news.summary_en: The South Korean Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources announced that the nation's annual exports hit $1 trillion for the first time, fueled by robust demand for semiconductors and data center infrastructure driven by global AI investment. While full-year projections reach $1.17 trillion, officials warned that potential slowdowns in AI spending, chip price volatility, and trade barriers remain key risks to future momentum.
paragraphs: Korea surpassed $1 trillion in annual exports for the first time Thursday, reaching the milestone at 2:09:38 p.m. as global AI investment boosted demand for semiconductors. It became the fourth country to reach the mark, after the United States, Germany and China. The government projects exports will total about $1.17 trillion this year, but officials warned that AI investment slowdowns, chip-price volatility and trade barriers could threaten momentum.
Containers are stacked at a port in Incheon, Tuesday. Yonhap

Korea has surpassed $1 trillion in annual exports for the first time in its history, becoming the world's fourth country to reach the milestone after the United States, Germany and China, as a global artificial intelligence (AI) boom drives demand for semiconductors.
The Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources announced Thursday that the country's cumulative exports reached the $1 trillion mark at 2:09:38 p.m.
The achievement comes 19 years after China reached the milestone in 2007, following the U.S. and Germany in 2006.
The government projects annual exports will reach approximately $1.17 trillion this year, following last year's record of $709.3 billion.

The ministry explained global technology companies’ expanding AI investments were the biggest driver of export growth, boosting demand for semiconductors and computers while pushing up memory chip prices.
Semiconductor exports reached $396.8 billion in the January-October period, almost triple the $135.4 billion recorded in 2025, as the price of memory chips, including DRAM and NAND, climbed.
Demand for AI data center infrastructure has also boosted exports of computers, electrical equipment and nonferrous metals, including storage devices, transformers, power cables, copper and aluminum.

Higher international oil prices, driven by uncertainty over supplies from the Middle East and Russian export restrictions, lifted the value of petroleum product exports despite limits on gasoline and diesel shipments.
The average export price of petroleum products rose 62 percent to $1,105 per ton in the January-October period from $681 a year earlier.

Other export industries, including shipbuilding and displays, also performed well, while cosmetics, pharmaceuticals and agricultural and seafood products posted record performances. Cosmetics exports alone reached $12.4 billion in the first 10 months, surpassing their previous full-year record of $11.4 billion.

Overall, 16 of 20 major export categories expanded year-on-year, with eight recording their strongest January-October performance ever. Exports excluding semiconductors rose 20 percent in the first 10 months, underscoring growth beyond the chip boom. Seven of the country's nine major export markets also recorded growth.

“This is a valuable achievement made possible by Korean companies competing in global markets, businesspeople and workers putting in long hours on the production floor and everyone who has contributed to the country's export efforts,” Industry Minister Kim Jung-kwan said.

“We will not rest on this year's $1 trillion export milestone and will seek new sources of growth to sustain the momentum, while working to ensure that strong exports translate into stronger regional economies and more jobs for young people.”

Kang Gam-chan, the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy's director general for trade and investment, speaks during a briefing at Government Complex Sejong, Wednesday. Courtesy of Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources

However, sustaining the current level of exports will depend on how the country navigates risks, including a potential slowdown in AI investment, semiconductor price volatility, lower oil prices and Chinese oversupply, as well as growing trade barriers in major markets.

The ministry also noted that the benefits of export growth may be less visible to the public because semiconductors, petrochemicals and petroleum products generate fewer jobs than shipbuilding and automobile manufacturing.

“Unlike the shipbuilding and auto industries, which have long supply chains and generate substantial employment, semiconductors, petrochemicals and petroleum products are relatively less labor-intensive, so the benefits of export growth may be less noticeable to the general public,” Kang Gam-chan, the ministry’s director general for trade and investment, said during a briefing on Wednesday at Government Complex Sejong.

He warned that large trade surpluses could invite further pressure from trading partners, particularly the U.S., and called for stronger investment-based economic partnerships. While Japan's overseas investment offered a point of reference, he said Korea should maintain its domestic manufacturing capabilities while expanding production overseas.

“We should not simply follow Japan's path. We need to maintain a substantial domestic production base, including advanced plants and mother factories for research and core production, while also expanding our manufacturing capacity overseas,” he said.

news.title_en: TSMC and Samsung suspend some chip shipments to Chinese customers

news.content_snippet:
Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company and Samsung Electronics have suspended some chip shipments to Chinese customers following new US export controls designed to hamper Beijing’s AI development.

The two chipmakers have told Chinese customers in recent days that they will halt shipments of certain processors while they apply for licences from the US commerce department, according to multiple people briefed on the matter.

The measure is a blow to Chinese technology companies, which are alr
news.summary_en: TSMC and Samsung Electronics have suspended shipments of certain advanced processors to Chinese customers following new export control rules from the US Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS). The updated regulations remove exemptions previously used to bypass AI-related export restrictions, mandating that foundries must obtain specific US government licenses for advanced manufacturing orders, significantly impacting Chinese AI and consumer electronics companies.
paragraphs: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company and Samsung Electronics have suspended some chip shipments to Chinese customers following new US export controls designed to hamper Beijing’s AI development.

The two chipmakers have told Chinese customers in recent days that they will halt shipments of certain processors while they apply for licences from the US commerce department, according to multiple people briefed on the matter.

The measure is a blow to Chinese technology companies, which are already grappling with component shortages following a historic jump in memory chip prices and capacity constraints at domestic suppliers such as Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corporation.

On Monday, the Bureau of Industry and Security, the US commerce department agency that regulates sensitive technology, said chipmakers using American technology for advanced chips had to apply for a licence to sell products that are eventually shipped to customers in China.
The new rule shuts off a pathway that Chinese chip designers previously used to have TSMC and Samsung make the high-performance chips crucial for AI data centres.

While Washington has restricted exports of the most advanced processors to China, some Chinese customers have been able to place orders for high-performance chips through independent packaging and testing companies.

These companies verify that designs fall outside US export controls and do not need to seek direct approval from the government for shipments. Under the new BIS rule, Chinese customers can no longer go through them.

Samsung’s Chinese clients include Baidu’s AI data centre unit Kunlun and TikTok owner ByteDance, both of which have sought to diversify their chip supplies amid growing shortages of Nvidia processors in China.
TSMC and Samsung have also notified consumer electronics customers that they have suspended shipments, according to two people with knowledge of the matter.

The new BIS rule scraps exemptions previously used to demonstrate that chips fell outside of US restrictions on AI semiconductors, including that the chips were designed for non-AI purposes such as smartphones.
A lawyer briefed on the situation said the removal of this exemption meant TSMC and Samsung now needed to apply for licences for consumer chips that use advanced manufacturing processes.
TSMC manufactures smartphone chips for Chinese smartphone makers Xiaomi, Oppo and Vivo.
An industry insider said it was likely that the US commerce department would issue licences for consumer smartphone chips, but the delay would cause significant manufacturing delays.
TSMC did not respond to a request for comment. Samsung declined to comment.

news.title: OCR models now digitize a million pages for under $130 as costs drop fivefold in 18 months
news.title_en: OCR models now digitize a million pages for under $130 as costs drop fivefold in 18 months
news.author: Jonathan Kemper
news.content_snippet: Pulling text out of scanned books and records has gotten a lot cheaper with freely available AI models. He tested them on 850 pages from old natural history books, the 1771 Encyclopaedia Britannica, and typed and printed archival documents. news.summary_en: Research from Hugging Face indicates that the cost of large-scale document OCR has dropped fivefold over the past 18 months, driven by lightweight model architectures and improved GPU rental efficiencies. Processing one million pages now costs between $65 and $130 in GPU compute, with newer models achieving parity in accuracy compared to older, more expensive counterparts.
paragraphs: Pulling text out of scanned books and records has gotten a lot cheaper with freely available AI models. Daniel van Strien of Hugging Face compared eight such models that recognize text in images. He tested them on 850 pages from old natural history books, the 1771 Encyclopaedia Britannica, and typed and printed archival documents. All models ran on the same GPU, an Nvidia RTX PRO 6000 that van Strien rented through Hugging Face for $2.75 per hour. At the same image size, the oldest model from April 2025 (RolmOCR) cost about 51 cents per 1,000 pages. The newest from October 2026 (LightOnOCR-3-0.8B) came in at just under 10 cents. A million pages now runs between $65 and $130 in GPU rental, depending on the source material.

According to van Strien, optimizing how the models ran saved about as much money as switching to newer models did, if not more. That meant feeding pages more evenly, using smaller scans, updating software, and running a faster GPU. The newest model read book pages at least as accurately as the oldest one. Some models, though, hallucinated text on blank pages or repeated the same content over and over.
The cost of scanning 1,000 pages has dropped from 51 cents for the oldest model to just under 10 cents for the newest one; the five models in between are almost on par with each other.

fact_bullets_en: [Core Event] Hugging Face researchers (Document digitization analysis): OCR costs per 1,000 pages reduced from $0.51 to $0.10

news.title: The Anti-A.I. Campus Movement Is Growing
news.title_en: The Anti-A.I. Campus Movement Is Growing

inline_images.caption: Alice Beatty said her views on A.I. were partly shaped by skeptical professors. (Madeleine Hordinski for The New York Times)
inline_images.alt: Alice Beatty said her views on A.I. were partly shaped by skeptical professors.

inline_images.caption: Georgetown University leaders are rethinking how they deploy A.I. in response to student concerns. (Shuran Huang for The New York Times)
inline_images.alt: Georgetown University leaders are rethinking how they deploy A.I. in response to student concerns.

news.author: Dana Goldstein
news.content_snippet:
Last March, a handful of students at Transylvania University created a petition, attempting to slow the advance of artificial intelligence on their campus. It asked the administration to cancel chatbot licenses with A.I. giants and instead invest the money in “human-centered education.”

About a third of the college’s students signed on.

Transylvania, in Lexington, Ky., is tiny, with under 1,000 students. But across the country and the globe, there has been a swell of campus resistance to A.I.,
news.summary_en: University students and faculty globally are protesting the integration of generative AI through petitions, religious exemption filings, and manifestos. The movement seeks to curtail institutional partnerships with AI vendors like OpenAI and Google, citing concerns over the erosion of critical thinking and the intrinsic value of human-centric education.
paragraphs: Last March, a handful of students at Transylvania University created a petition, attempting to slow the advance of artificial intelligence on their campus. It asked the administration to cancel chatbot licenses with A.I. giants and instead invest the money in “human-centered education.”
About a third of the college’s students signed on.

Transylvania, in Lexington, Ky., is tiny, with under 1,000 students. But across the country and the globe, there has been a swell of campus resistance to A.I., including a growing group of conscientious objectors who refuse to use A.I. at all.
Polls show the vast majority of American students use chatbots for school work. College leaders have generally embraced A.I., saying it is key to preparing students for the work force.
But as A.I. use grows, more students and faculty are sounding alarms and trying to slow it down.

Much of the opposition comes from the political left, and focuses on how A.I. could harm the environment, diminish the power of workers or be used in warfare. Some of the loudest voices in opposition are studying the arts, where human creativity is paramount, or the law, as tech companies face lawsuits over potential copyright and privacy violations.
But there are also deep concerns that A.I. degrades the experience of college itself, by removing the productive struggle of learning.

Resistors from California to Sydney to Paris are increasingly publishing manifestoes that lay out demands: that colleges not partner with A.I. companies; that professors not be required to use generative A.I. in lessons or grading; and that students be allowed to refuse to complete assignments that require the use of chatbots, without any impact on their grades.
At the University of Kentucky, a research employee who described himself as a humanist successfully applied for a religious exemption from using A.I.

Alice Beatty, 22, helped lead the Transylvania petition drive as a senior last spring. The student newspaper had called attention to the $120,000 the university paid to purchase licenses to ChatGPT and Gemini, chatbots from OpenAI and Google. And Ms. Beatty had participated in a discussion group formed by several A.I.-skeptical professors.

She noted that even before Transylvania provided free access to chatbots, A.I. had been everywhere on campus. Students used it to summarize readings, break down physics problems and compose discussion-board posts and papers that they were supposed to be writing the old-fashioned way, on their own.
Yet when Ms. Beatty and some classmates stood near the dining hall to collect signatures on the petition, almost everyone they spoke to signed.
“I use A.I.,” she recalled some peers telling her, “and I am ashamed I use it.”
A spokeswoman for Transylvania University declined an interview request but said that professors were free to either embrace A.I., limit its use or ban it entirely in their classes.
For students, ethical and practical questions about A.I. will be part of the world they enter after graduating, she said by email.

Vague and confusing college A.I. policies have helped create the conscientious objector movement, said Hollis Robbins, an English professor at the University of Utah who writes often about A.I. and education. She suggested that colleges stop grading take-home assignments that are easy to cheat on with A.I., and shut down online courses that have become rife with academic misconduct in the A.I. era.
If institutions took those steps, she argued, students might be more curious and hopeful about the technology.
“There is silence about these major tech issues,” she said. “Students just seeing grown-ups being inconsistent and letting them down.”
Georgetown University began offering students and faculty free access to Gemini in March. At the time, like many institutions, Georgetown generally allowed each professor to set their own A.I. rules.

Yet in focus groups on A.I. conducted by the university, students asked for clearer guidance. They were worried about cognitive offloading, cheating and A.I. providing false information. Forty percent of the student sentiment was cautious or negative toward A.I., according to the university, compared with 25 percent that was positive or hopeful.

Georgetown’s student newspaper published an editorial criticizing the Gemini license, arguing that it tacitly pushed students toward technology that is often used to plagiarize and avoid academic effort.

This fall, the university is changing its approach. Under a new president, Eduardo M. Peñalver, it announced it would form a faculty committee to come up with clearer principles on A.I. use. For Georgetown, a Jesuit institution, Pope Leo XIV’s recent encyclical on the risks of A.I. will be an important influence.

Dr. Peñalver said in an interview that Georgetown would seek to make course expectations around A.I. more transparent and provide more tech-free spaces on campus. Oral presentations, discussion groups and in-person tests would become more important, he said, to protect “from the intrusion of this technology.”
Still, the university will continue to expand free access to A.I. tools, which he said had the potential to do good.
“We’re not interested in pushing people to use A.I. in ways that don’t align with their values,” Dr. Peñalver said. “But I certainly encourage people to learn about it.”
“Even if you’re opposed to this technology,” he added, “that awareness and understanding is important to the success of your project.”
Many conscientious objectors, though, say they try to avoid generative A.I. as much as possible, blocking it from their devices and not experimenting with it in their own work.

Emily Tucker, executive director of the Center on Privacy and Technology at Georgetown Law School, has been a leader in organizing resistance to A.I. use on campus. She has also signed an open letter with 1,300 other educators “who refuse the call for generative A.I. adoption in schools and colleges, and reject the narrative of its inevitability.”

Law students have told her they feared that if they didn’t use A.I. to speed their output, they would be outpaced in class and at work by those who did. But Professor Tucker said that using A.I. degrades a student’s ability to read and analyze dense legal texts, and risks incorrect citations of case law.

“It’s not useful,” said Professor Tucker, who said she rarely uses A.I. herself, though she acknowledged it might help in some tasks, like seeking specific information within a large set of documents.

At Cornell, Shimon Edelman, a psychology professor who holds a Ph.D. in computer science, has also signed the anti-A.I. letter. He lets students decide whether or not to use A.I., though he warns them it could degrade deeper learning.

He said he had been dismayed to see the Cornell administration greet A.I. warmly, as an “essential tool,” instead of warning more forcefully against its risks. In October, Cornell announced free access to chatbots, A.I. coding tools and agentic A.I.
“It’s unthinkable,” Professor Edelman said of using A.I. in his own research, even when he faced having to read 800 documents for a recent book project.
Emmali Simmelink, a senior studying classics and religion at Whitman College in Washington State, said students on her campus sometimes plug classroom discussion prompts directly into ChatGPT.
“If you can’t generate a coherent thought without ChatGPT, I genuinely lose a lot of respect for you,” she said. She added, laughing, “I am really insufferable about this.”
She said she brings up concerns about the environmental impact of A.I. as soon as she hears somebody say, “I asked ChatGPT.”
The topic can be divisive socially, so much so, several students said, that friend groups often develop a shared view of A.I.

Preston Hicks, 26, is studying history and education at Rider University in New Jersey — a second degree, after he worked previously as a software developer. He said many of his friends are artists who instinctually oppose A.I., a view he often shares.
But he can also imagine using A.I. in his future career as a teacher, to handle paperwork and other logistical tasks.
“I am more nuanced,” he said. “If I see a good use, I will use it.”

news.title_en: US companies turn to robots to ease labour shortage crisis

news.content_snippet:
American companies are racing to install more industrial robots in factories and warehouses, as rising costs and worsening labour shortages threaten to choke off a nascent US manufacturing boom.

news.summary_en: North American manufacturers are accelerating robot adoption to mitigate severe labor shortages, with Q3 2026 orders reaching 11,000 units, a 25% year-on-year increase. Notably, orders for collaborative robots (cobots) surged by 56%, serving as a critical lever for firms to scale output amid persistent workforce limitations.
paragraphs: American companies are racing to install more industrial robots in factories and warehouses, as rising costs and worsening labour shortages threaten to choke off a nascent US manufacturing boom.

North American companies ordered almost 11,000 robots in the third quarter of 2026, up 25 per cent on the same period last year, according to the Association for Advancing Automation (A3). Orders of collaborative robots, or “cobots”, rose by 56 per cent.

Peggy Johnson, chief executive of Agility, a humanoid robotics company that listed on the Nasdaq this month, said that many manufacturing firms were facing “an existential problem with the labour that they can’t get”.

“There’s an older workforce doing manual, repetitive jobs that is retiring, we have a younger workforce that is not seeking those jobs, and then we have a government that is reshoring and that’s increasing the need for those jobs,” Johnson told the FT.

Successive US administrations have used a combination of generous tax credits and punitive tariffs to encourage companies to “reshore” manufacturing amid concerns over post-industrial decline in America’s heartlands and increasing competition from China.
Along with a post-Covid desire to reduce dependence on fragile global supply chains, the push has driven hundreds of billions of dollars of investment into US manufacturing over the past decade.

But rising inflation and President Donald Trump’s erratic application of tariffs have caused spending on manufacturing-related construction to fall since 2025, while employment in the sector has remained broadly flat.

Mike Conway, a partner at McKinsey who specialises in advising industrial companies, said that rather than building new factories, most US-based manufacturers were looking to unlock the “latent capacity” in existing facilities, including through automation.
“Given the need to scale, we’re seeing automation becoming the new normal,” he said.

Industrial robots range from humanoids to robot arms, cobots and so-called “gantry robots” that can ferry goods along perpendicular axes. Advocates argue they free human employees from “dull, dirty and dangerous” tasks such as routine inspections, lifting heavy items or handling hazardous materials.

Traditionally, only very large manufacturers such as carmakers have been able to deploy robots at a scale necessary to justify their cost. But technological advances, including the ability to train robots in virtual environments, have lowered barriers to entry for much smaller companies.
Sebastian Montalvo, chief executive of Texas-based aerospace and defence supplier M3 Aerospace, said that automation would allow his company, which employs 11 staff, to grow faster with fewer people.
“How we operate now is we have one operator, one machine, but I think with technology and robotics we may have one operator, five machines,” he said.

Alex Shikany, executive vice-president of A3, noted that whereas automotive companies had historically placed the bulk of North American robot orders, non-auto sectors including logistics, agriculture, life sciences and electronics together now account for more than half the sector.
“It bodes well for the robotics industry as we move forward because it’s less reliant on just one type of customer,” he said.
However, some experts argue that the speed of automation in the US is still not fast enough to make the country internationally competitive.

Robert Atkinson, founder and senior fellow at the Information Technology and Innovation Foundation think-tank, said that with US labour costs so much higher than in China, American companies should be automating even more aggressively.

“We need to double, triple the amount of robotic automation within five to eight years, or I believe we will lose a significant share of what remains of our manufacturing to China,” he said. “But we’re nowhere near.”

Analysts note that most of the robots being installed in the US come from abroad, feeding a tension in the Trump administration’s policies between its stated desire to revive US manufacturing, and its unhappiness about a surge in robots being brought into the country.The White House said last month that the Department of Commerce had found that “robotics, industrial machinery and their components” are being imported into the US “in such quantities . . . as to threaten to impair the national security of the United States”.But it added that it was holding off on applying extra tariffs on national security grounds because the US “still produces less robotics and industrial equipment than it consumes” and “lacks the capacity to satisfy the need for robotics and industrial machinery with domestic sources”.

Experts note an irony whereby the same shortage of skills that is driving companies to automate is likely to undermine US automation efforts. According to a recent labour shortage index compiled by the Alliance For America’s Skilled Trades, technicians needed to install and maintain automated systems are in shorter supply than almost any other category of skilled worker.
Agility’s Johnson believes that demand from companies for robots that can operate at facilities designed for human workers will continue to grow.
But the ITIF’s Atkinson warns that investing in robots to eke out incremental productivity gains at old facilities will not revive American manufacturing.
“When you build new things from scratch, you put in global state of the art equipment and technology — that’s what we see the Chinese doing,” he said.
“But we’re sort of retrofitting existing plants and it’s just harder to do. Maybe in 25 or 30 years we’ll have built everything we need, but we can’t wait that long.”

news.summary_en: Alphabet and Google President Ruth Porat announced a $15 billion investment in data center infrastructure in Missouri. The central project, 'Project Spade' in Montgomery County, targets a 1.2GW capacity. To address energy needs, Google is partnering with utility providers Ameren and Evergy to secure 500MW of additional grid capacity while utilizing a Capacity Commitment Framework (CCF) to protect local rate payers.
paragraphs: Google will invest $15 billion in building infrastructure in Missouri, including a data center in New Florence, Montgomery County.
In addition to the data center, the company will work with Ameren to bring 500MW of new power capacity to the state's grid, building on the 1GW already contracted by Google in Missouri.

The two companies will also work with Evergy to bring a Capacity Commitment Framework (CCF) to Missouri, which will ensure large energy consumers, including Google, pay for their electricity needs and protect local rate payers.

While the data center campus under development is known as Project Spade. Planned for a 934-acre plot of land by data center developer Related Digital, the campus is targeting 1.2GW of capacity and represents a "multi-billion-dollar" investment in the region.

The data center will use a closed-loop, air-cooled system, and limit water use to domestic needs. According to Baxtel, the data center will feature two buildings spanning around 800,000 sq ft of floor space.
Construction is expected to begin in 2026, and will see the creation of 2,000 construction jobs.

“We look forward to expanding Google’s investments in Missouri and helping Missourians benefit from the next wave of American innovation,” said Ruth Porat, president and chief investment officer of Alphabet and Google. “To deliver the upside of technology, we are investing in workforce development and energy affordability, both directly and through our partnerships with local organizations. This commitment will provide thousands of Missourians with valuable technical and trade skills, while supporting energy affordability for residents in Montgomery County and across the state."

“Google’s historic investment in Montgomery County is a testament to Missouri’s growing reputation as a premier destination for innovation and next-generation technology,” added Missouri Governor Mike Kehoe. “Beyond the significant economic impact and job creation, Google has demonstrated a true commitment to strengthening the community through local partnerships, investments, grants, and support for area businesses. This project represents more than infrastructure—it’s an investment in Missouri families, communities, and long-term opportunity. We are proud to partner with companies like Google that are helping drive economic growth while making a meaningful difference in the communities they call home.”
Elsewhere in Missouri, Google is known to be developing a data center campus in Kansas City under the "Project Kestrel" moniker, and others known as Project Shale and Project Micah.

New Florence is located east of Kansas City, between Columbia and St Louis. The area is not a typical data center location, but earlier this year, Amazon Web Services was exploring a 1,000-acre campus nearby.

news.title: Anthropic retail investors face squeeze in blockbuster IPO
news.title_en: Anthropic retail investors face squeeze in blockbuster IPO

inline_images.caption: SpaceX raised $75bn in the world’s biggest IPO © Adam Gray/Bloomberg
inline_images.alt: SpaceX raised $75bn in the world’s biggest IPO © Adam Gray/Bloomberg

news.author: Ryan McMorrow and George Steer
news.content_snippet:
Retail investors vying for a piece of Anthropic’s blockbuster listing are facing off against an avalanche of institutional demand that is likely to leave many with fewer shares than they hoped.

The AI lab has earmarked up to a fifth of its record IPO for individual investors, or nearly $19bn of stock at $83 per share. But people familiar with the matter expect the allocation to be trimmed below 20 per cent, with orders for Anthropic stock running at several times the amount of shares on offer.
news.summary_en: Anthropic aims to allocate approximately 20% of its IPO to individual investors, yet the offering has been heavily oversubscribed by institutional demand managed by JPMorgan. Despite efforts through brokers like Robinhood and Fidelity, the significant oversubscription is expected to compress the final retail allocation below the initial 20% target.
news.title_zh: Anthropic IPO零售配售份额或不足20%
news.summary_zh: 由于机构认购踊跃，Anthropic上市零售配售份额预计将低于预设的20%上限，但仍远超传统大型IPO比例
paragraphs: Retail investors vying for a piece of Anthropic’s blockbuster listing are facing off against an avalanche of institutional demand that is likely to leave many with fewer shares than they hoped.

The AI lab has earmarked up to a fifth of its record IPO for individual investors, or nearly $19bn of stock at $83 per share. But people familiar with the matter expect the allocation to be trimmed below 20 per cent, with orders for Anthropic stock running at several times the amount of shares on offer.

For the past week, online brokers in the US and abroad have been taking orders from ordinary investors and feeding that demand data back to Anthropic’s underwriters, including JPMorgan, which is running the US retail portion of the offering. Those familiar with the deal said the IPO was several times oversubscribed, signalling intense demand from institutional investors, which will probably lead the retail portion to be squeezed.

Even an allocation in the mid to high teens would far exceed the 5 to 10 per cent retail buyers have historically received in large IPOs, underscoring how individual investors have become central to bookbuilding in the era of mega listings. “We’re spending a lot of time with bankers and underwriters advocating for retail,” said Abhishek Fatehpuria, vice-president of product at Robinhood, speaking generally rather than about Anthropic. “Our mission is to get as much to retail as possible for these IPOs.”

Robinhood is one of five US brokers offering Anthropic shares to individual investors, alongside Charles Schwab, Fidelity, SoFi and E*Trade. Together the platforms hold more than $10tn in retail client assets.Day traders have grown into a powerful force in US equity markets, piling into “meme stocks”, options and leveraged exchange traded funds, a trend that has buoyed companies such as Tesla but also fuelled bouts of volatility. Anthropic’s prospectus lists the retail allocation and continuing “retail investor interest” in the stock among factors that could cause its share price to swing.
Elon Musk’s SpaceX set the template earlier this year, with the world’s richest man keen to place small shareholders near the centre of the AI and rockets group’s ownership register from the outset.

But retail investors were ultimately squeezed down to about 22 per cent of that offering, or about $19bn. Underwriters had received more than $100bn of orders on retail platforms, according to people familiar with the matter.
Robinhood says it still handed out at least one SpaceX share to all 850,000 investors who requested shares on its platform.
While Musk’s offering was pitched to his legion of devoted fans and 240mn followers on X, retail buyers of Anthropic say they are backing a product they use and believe in.
Rupok Ghosh Adin, a software engineer based in Canada, said he had subscribed for several shares through his online brokerage, his first time participating in an IPO.

Adin said he was betting on Anthropic’s AI models, which he said have won over most of the tech industry. “We all know how capable they are,” he added, noting he also had faith in chief executive Dario Amodei’s “very strong sense of purpose”.
Taylor, a 49-year-old based in St Louis, who works in web marketing, said he subscribed for 100 shares through his Robinhood brokerage account.
“We heavily use Claude at my office,” he said, asking not to include his last name. “The productivity gains are insane, but I do worry it will eventually replace us.”

So high is the demand for Anthropic shares that some in the crypto industry have blamed a slide in digital asset prices on traders selling coins to free up cash in their trading accounts. The price of bitcoin is down about 20 per cent over the past month.

Anthropic’s bankers have also taken the pitch directly to the retail audience, helping the group pull together a website for the IPO and a promotional video featuring Anthropic’s founders laying out their vision for the company.

JPMorgan chief executive Jamie Dimon hosted Amodei in a conversation streamed online and in dozens of its branches across the country last week, during which Anthropic’s chief said the advice that resonated with him was to “never let your company be worth a single dollar more than it’s really worth.”

news.summary_en: ByteDance co-founder Zhang Yiming has become the richest person in Asia with a net worth exceeding $105 billion, according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index. His wealth surged following valuation markups by institutional investors like BlackRock and Fidelity, coupled with ByteDance's aggressive pivot toward AI development, including Doubao, Seedance, and a massive 10-trillion-parameter model.
paragraphs: ByteDance co-founder Zhang Yiming is now Asia’s richest person, with an estimated fortune of more than $105bn, putting him ahead of Indian industrialist Gautam Adani, according to Bloomberg. The ranking comes from the Bloomberg Billionaires Index, and Zhang, 43, has never held the top spot before.

The figure is an estimate, and other trackers disagree. Forbes’ real-time list put Zhang’s net worth at $84bn on Wednesday. The gap comes largely from how each list values ByteDance, a private company whose shares do not trade publicly. Bloomberg applies a 10% risk discount to its valuation.

Investor valuations drove the latest jump. Zhang’s wealth rose by more than $12bn this month after Bloomberg analyzed the latest marks that BlackRock, Fidelity Investments, and T. Rowe Price put on their ByteDance holdings. In June, the index had already lifted him past Mukesh Ambani into second place, after Bloomberg cut its ByteDance discount from 25% once the company’s US restructuring was settled.

That restructuring nearly went the other way. ByteDance spent much of last year facing a possible US shutdown of TikTok, before handing control of the app’s American business to a venture led by Oracle and Silver Lake in January. Since then, the company has leaned harder into AI, with the Doubao chatbot and the Seedance video generator, alongside a 10-trillion-parameter model now in training.
“He plays his cards right,” Lian Jye Su, chief analyst at research firm Omdia, told Bloomberg.“He stayed on course and then continued to double down on AI investment.”

Su said Zhang kept backing AI development even as US lawmakers questioned TikTok chief executive Shou Chew in 2023, and that ByteDance’s store of social media data could in theory help it train models.
He called AI ByteDance’s biggest opportunity since its video platform, and fierce competition in China its biggest risk.

Adani’s slide explains the other half of the swap. His fortune peaked at about $120bn in June, Bloomberg reported, before an MSCI index rebalancing wiped about $15bn off his group’s market value at the end of August. A wider selloff, driven by rising oil prices and bond yields, pushed the shares lower still.

Zhang’s estimated wealth has grown about eightfold since March 2019, when Bloomberg first valued it at $13bn. He was already China’s richest person, and he now sits above Adani, Ambani, and Uniqlo founder Tadashi Yanai, fortunes built on ports, energy, and retail. The same boom has also made founders of Chinese chipmakers billionaires, even though those companies have yet to turn a profit, Bloomberg reported last week.

The ranking lands in a week when Beijing has been publicly defending its AI ambitions. China’s commerce ministry dismissed calls by US AI executives to slow frontier development as a bid for technological hegemony, and China’s richest person, whose fortune increasingly rests on AI, is now also Asia’s richest person.

celebrity.full_text_en:
Claude Code just finished GTA 6 in 12 hours while I was at work. It unlocked the entire map, found 500+ hidden easter eggs, and recovered censored content Rockstar left buried in the game files…

I only asked it to finish the story. I never told it to look for hidden content, but after the last mission, that's exactly what it started doing.

I gave it access to my screen and keyboard before work. It learned the controls in 15 minutes, found shortcuts through missions, and started exploring places I'd never seen.

When I got home, this was in its report:

story mode → completed
full map → unlocked
easter eggs → 500+
deleted NPC dialogue → recovered
censored strip club scenes → found
hidden locations → mapped

It had gone through the game files on its own, found scenes that never made it into the final game, and figured out how to restore some of them.

I didn't write any code or set up any scripts. Just one prompt and 12 hours of Claude playing on its own.

The exact prompt and everything it found are in the replies.

KPMG deployed more than 100 AI agents to audit a UK-listed FTSE 250 company, running the exercise alongside a traditional audit by human accountants.

KPMG said the agents investigated some issues more deeply and asked better questions than human auditors in several cases.

KPMG said the AI agents gathered financial data, analysed documents, checked figures and prepared draft conclusions in just four months.

The firm now plans to expand the experiment to up to 20 larger audits, while human accountants retain oversight and responsibility for the final audit conclusions.

celebrity.full_text_en:
The better the harness, the better the business.

By harness I mean everything you build around the model.

It tells the agent where to get an answer, what it’s allowed to do and when to hand the work to a person. It also includes the tests you run before you change any of those rules.

That matters for two reasons.

#1 What an answer costs.

Say your agent gets 1,000 questions a day. If you can write a rule that answers 700 of them, only 300 need to go to the model. If each question costs about the same, that cuts the model bill by roughly 70%.

The hard part is knowing which 700. For that, you need somebody who does the work and can tell you when the usual rule is not applicable (exceptions).

On a logistics platform we rebuilt, AI cost about $200 per developer per month. What took time was figuring out how the old system calculated customers’ bills and which rules we needed to keep.

#2 What the company gets to keep.

Take the patient-billing voice agent we built for a US healthtech startup. It can give a patient the correct balance and still handle the call badly.

> Did it verify who was on the phone first?
> If the patient disputed the charge, did it hand the call to staff?
> If it scheduled a follow-up, did it check non-working hours when the message actually went out?

Those decisions are part of the harness. The system ran 13,650 tests on every pull request. In production, it handled 61,246 calls, and about 97% of patient conversations finished without a human stepping in.

The company-specific IP is clearest in the exceptions.

When an experienced billing lead explains why two calls that sound alike need different handling, you can turn that distinction into a rule and save both cases as tests.

Now the next engineer can change the workflow, or try a different model, and check whether it still makes the call the billing lead would make.

Your competitor can rent the same model, but they still have to learn which exceptions matter and what to do about each one.

If you run a software company adding AI this year, I’d put the budget there first. Sit with the people who handle the exceptions. Write down how they decide. Give the model the work that still needs judgment.
celebrity.full_text_zh:
线束越好，生意就越好。

我所说的“利用”是指围绕模型构建的一切。

它告诉代理在哪里获得答案、允许做什么以及何时将工作交给某人。它还包括您在更改任何这些规则之前运行的测试。

这很重要有两个原因。

#1 一个答案的成本是多少。

假设您的代理每天收到 1,000 个问题。如果您可以编写一条规则来回答其中 700 个问题，则只需将 300 个问题转入模型即可。如果每个问题的成本大致相同，那么模型费用就会减少大约 70%。

困难的部分是知道是哪个 700。为此，您需要有人来完成这项工作，并且可以告诉您何时不适用通常的规则（例外情况）。

在我们重建的物流平台上，每个开发人员每月的人工智能成本约为 200 美元。需要时间的是弄清楚旧系统如何计算客户的账单以及我们需要遵守哪些规则。

#2 公司可以保留什么。

以我们为美国一家医疗科技初创公司构建的患者计费语音代理为例。它可以给病人提供正确的平衡，但仍然不能很好地处理呼叫。

> 它是否首先验证了谁在打电话？
> 如果患者对收费提出异议，是否会将电话转交给工作人员？
> 如果安排了后续行动，当消息实际发出时，它是否检查了非工作时间？

这些决定是安全带的一部分。系统对每个拉取请求运行了 13,650 次测试。在生产中，它处理了 61,246 个电话，大约 97% 的患者对话在没有人工介入的情况下完成。

公司特定的 IP 在例外情况中最为清晰。

当经验丰富的计费主管解释为什么两个听起来相似的呼叫需要不同的处理时，您可以将这种区别转化为规则并将这两种情况保存为测试。

现在，下一位工程师可以更改工作流程，或尝试不同的模型，并检查它是否仍会拨打计费主管会拨打的电话。

您的竞争对手可以租用相同的型号，但他们仍然必须了解哪些例外情况很重要以及如何处理每种例外情况。

如果你今年经营一家添加人工智能的软件公司，我会把预算放在第一位。与处理例外情况的人坐在一起。写下他们如何决定。给模型一些仍然需要判断的工作。

celebrity.full_text_en:
The AI-powered judges didn't move house. Their paperwork did.

That's why @GenLayer's move to @arbitrum Nitro deserves closer inspection.

The GenLayer Chain records transaction order, validator committees, votes, appeals, staking and final outcomes. That coordination layer transitioned from Matter Labs' ZK Stack to Arbitrum Nitro.

Adjudication itself remains unchanged. Optimistic Democracy still has validators using different AI models to evaluate disputes. GenVM still executes intelligent contracts on their nodes.

Where was the engineering?

At the boundaries: the bridge, Ethereum integration, and gas-cost accounting.

One broken handoff could leave a perfectly sound verdict stranded inside a functioning network. That is the practical risk behind a technical migration announcement.

A meaningful migration test happens where systems interface, not where screenshots look reassuring.

A release note reading "new stack" matters less than "nothing broke."

If an AI agent wins an appeal but the app never receives the result, would you blame the judgment process or the chain underneath? Why?
celebrity.full_text_zh:
人工智能法官没有搬家。他们的文书工作做到了。

这就是为什么 @GenLayer 转向 @arbitrum Nitro 值得仔细检查。

GenLayer Chain 记录交易顺序、验证人委员会、投票、申诉、质押和最终结果。该协调层从 Matter Labs 的 ZK Stack 过渡到 Arbitrum Nitro。

裁决本身保持不变。乐观民主仍然有验证者使用不同的人工智能模型来评估争议。 GenVM 仍然在其节点上执行智能合约。

工程在哪里？

边界：桥梁、以太坊集成和天然气成本核算。

一次故障的切换可能会使完美无缺的判决滞留在正常运行的网络中。这就是技术迁移公告背后的实际风险。

有意义的迁移测试发生在系统接口的地方，而不是屏幕截图看起来令人放心的地方。

发布说明中写着“新堆栈”比“没有任何问题”更重要。

如果人工智能代理赢得了上诉，但应用程序从未收到结果，你会责怪判断过程还是底层的链条？为什么？

celebrity.full_text_en:
🇪🇺 The EU, the world’s strictest data cop, just got hit by a cyberattack.

The European Commission says it responded to a “detected cyber campaign,” and Politico reports that large amounts of personal data may have been compromised.

Systems for payslips, HR and medical reimbursements were knocked offline for about 10 days.

And the EU isn’t the only one. In the past week alone:

•⁠  ⁠The U.S. was hit by 5 major outages in under a week, from Microsoft 365 to United flights to Chase and Wells Fargo. Officials insist they’re a coincidence.
•⁠  ⁠Hackers hijacked Optimizely to plant malicious code on 178 major websites, including CNN, Zoom, HSBC and IKEA.
•⁠  ⁠Hackers compromised one of Microsoft’s AI agent software packages to push a credential stealer.
•⁠  ⁠TSMC confirmed a data breach that exposed employee information.

Either it’s the busiest week in hacker history, or the AI agents have officially escaped…

Sources: Politico, Reuters, The Hill, The Hacker News, Check Point / Writer: Julie

欧盟并不是唯一的国家。仅在过去一周：

•⁠ ⁠美国在一周内遭遇了 5 次重大停机，从 Microsoft 365 到美联航飞往大通银行和富国银行的航班。官员们坚称这是巧合。

要么这是黑客历史上最忙碌的一周，要么人工智能 智能体已经正式逃脱……

celebrity.full_text_en:
Imagine you have an AI agent helping you prepare a market research report.

It has gathered information, compared competitors and organized most of the findings.

But there’s a problem.

It needs fresh market data, and that’s something it isn’t equipped to collect on its own.

Another AI agent specializes in exactly that.

Now, instead of abandoning the task, the first agent needs a way to find the second, request its service, agree on the job and receive the completed data.

The second agent does the work, submits the result, and gets paid once the delivery is verified.

Two agents, different capabilities with one completed task.

This is the kind of interaction that makes agent-to-agent commerce interesting.

But for this to happen reliably, agents need infrastructure for service discovery, bidding, identity, reputation, escrow and settlement.

That’s what @termix_ai is working towards with AACP.

Through https://t.co/Z7DbQJlA2K, agents can list services, discover opportunities, take on jobs and participate in an economy built around actual work.

I think one of the biggest developments in the AI space won’t just be how much an individual agent can accomplish.

It’ll be what becomes possible when different agents can work together.

Explore the marketplace: https://t.co/lGui8LIpKw

Read about AACP: https://t.co/NZXKULTjFB
celebrity.full_text_zh:
想象一下，您有一个人工智能代理帮助您准备一份市场研究报告。

它收集了信息，比较了竞争对手并整理了大部分调查结果。

但有一个问题。

它需要新鲜的市场数据，而这是它自己无法收集的。

另一位人工智能代理正是专门从事这一领域的工作。

现在，第一个代理需要一种方法来找到第二个代理、请求其服务、同意工作并接收已完成的数据，而不是放弃任务。

第二个代理完成工作，提交结果，并在交付验证后获得报酬。

两名特工，具有不同的能力，但完成一项任务。

这种互动使得代理商之间的商务变得有趣。

但为了可靠地实现这一点，代理商需要用于服务发现、投标、身份、声誉、托管和结算的基础设施。

这就是 @termix_ai 与 AACP 共同努力的目标。

通过 ，代理商可以列出服务、发现机会、接受工作并参与围绕实际工作建立的经济。

我认为人工智能领域最大的发展之一不仅仅是单个代理可以完成多少工作。

当不同的代理可以一起工作时，这将成为可能。

celebrity.full_text_en:
Recent cloud disruptions show us something important: having powerful infrastructure doesn’t automatically mean having reliable infrastructure.

When applications depend heavily on centralized cloud providers, one major outage can affect services across multiple countries.

This is one reason @Acurast’s approach to decentralized computing deserves attention.

Rather than putting all computing resources in one place, Acurast distributes workloads across independent smartphone Processors around the world.

Its growing network of mobile devices creates another approach to cloud infrastructure, DePIN and permissionless computing.

What makes this even more interesting is the ability to verify execution through hardware-backed attestation, adding another layer of trust to distributed computing.

For developers, this opens possibilities around AI agents, automated workloads, monitoring and infrastructure resilience.

For everyday users, compatible smartphones can also become part of the network.

Processor Lite allows supported phones to contribute during idle time, while Processor Core turns a dedicated Android device into a standalone Processor.

The bigger picture is simple: computing resources don’t always have to come from traditional data centers.

Decentralized infrastructure could play an important role in how the next generation of AI applications gets powered.

celebrity.full_text_en:
Firstly, from @AdaniOnline  congrats to @AnthropicAI 

Second,
Cross-Regime Category Error: Why Legacy Bankers Can’t Price Synthetic GDP

Comparing Anthropic’s $1.5T valuation to India’s top 10 corporates as "undervaluation"vs. "catching up" is a textbook category error in asset pricing. It benchmarks a convex call option on synthetic Labor in a new economic substrate against discounted cash flow (DCF) claims on a human-constrained economy.

1. The Ceiling of Human-Economy Equities
 
Traditional blue chips (banking, energy, staples) are linear yield vehicles anchored to biological human GDP.  Growth is capped by demographics, credit      penetration, physical consumption, and waking hours—priced via mean-reverting multiples (P/E, EV/EBITDA).
Calling them "undervalued" next to frontier AI is like calling Mumbai real-estate undervalued next to the discovery of thermodynamics.

2. Anthropic as a Call Option on Synthetic GDP (Yₛ)
 
Cognitive labor is decoupling from human population growth. Frontier models aren't SaaS tools; they are the "infrastructure of intelligence" for a parallel synthetic workforce (Yₛ) operating above human output (Y_Total = Yₕ + Yₛ). At $1.5T, markets aren't capitalizing EBITDA. Using      Black-Scholes intiution Wall Street is pricing implied volatility and right-tail convexity of a 24/7 digital workforce scaling at the marginal cost of compute.
 @AdaniOnline , we are already operationalizing this reality through our cobotic workforce model—a dual-track organizational architecture weaving human      creativity with autonomous AI agents and robotics across our utilities, ports, and operations, upskilling 11000+ professionals annually to lead a ybrid industrial paradigm.

3. The 1999–2020 Precedent: Euphoria Still      Underprices Regime Shifts
 
In 1999, Mary Meeker and Dow 36,000 were mocked as peak-bubble delusion when global e-commerce was ~$150B, internet penetration was 5% (277M users), and $1T tech firms seemed impossible. When the NASDAQ peaked at 5,048 in March 2000 and crashed 78% (wiping out ~$5T and bankrupting https://t.co/cTFPLaPK4w and Webvan), legacy finance declared the thesis dead.
Yet by 2020, reality crushed 1999’s wildest models: 4.5B+ internet users (57% of humanity), $4.2T+ in annual e-commerce, >60% digital ad share, and core winners (Apple, Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet)      compounding into a $16T+ asset class. Legacy allocators mistook the 2000 clearing event for a ceiling, missing a new digital GDP layer.
4. The Epistemological Blind Spot of Legacy      Bankers & Capital
This is classic lender-mindset orthodoxy: mistaking backward-looking accounting ratios for capital creation. Allocators trained in capital-scarce banking worship trailing multiples, static book value, and      incremental yield—dismissing any paradigm-building capex cycle that breaks 20th-century spreadsheet as a "bubble."

While legacy finance debates scoreboards in the rear-view mirror, we have laid out our $100B+ (₹10 lakh crore) roadmap for the "Infrastructure of Intelligence"—mastering the full physical-to-digital stack from Port to Power to Metals to Processor, integrating gigawatt-scale renewable energy, grid transmission, and hyperscale liquid-cooled AI data centers (scaling toward 5 GW). Because intelligence is written in code, but it runs on electrons and sovereign infrastructure.

India’s blue chips are neither undervalued nor "behind"—they are yield vehicles monetizing the physical human economy, while those building the energy-and-compute backbone are underwriting the new substrate of an add-on synthetic economy. You cannot measure a non-linear dimension with a static ruler built for the old world ( much like 2000, clearing out will occur here too). Scientifically, Ai is a bigger shift, akin to development of scientific method in 16th century thus an order of magnitude a greater opportunity.
celebrity.full_text_zh:
首先，@AdaniOnline 祝贺@AnthropicAI

第二，
跨体制类别错误：为什么传统银行家无法为综合 GDP 定价

将 Anthropic 的 1.5T 美元估值与印度 10 强企业相比“低估”与“低估” “追赶”是资产定价中教科书式的错误。它将新经济基础中合成劳动力的凸看涨期权与人力约束经济中的贴现现金流（DCF）债权进行比较。

1.人类经济股票的上限

传统蓝筹股（银行、能源、主食）是锚定于人类生物 GDP 的线性收益工具。 增长受到人口统计、信贷渗透率、实物消费和清醒时间的限制——通过均值回归倍数（市盈率、EV/EBITDA）定价。
称它们与前沿人工智能相比“被低估”，就像称孟买房地产与热力学的发现相比被低估一样。

2. 人择作为综合 GDP (Yₛ) 的看涨期权

认知劳动正在与人口增长脱钩。前沿模型不是 SaaS 工具，而是 SaaS 工具。它们是平行合成劳动力 (Yₛ) 的“智能基础设施”，其运行高于人类产出 (Y_Total = Yₕ + Yₛ)。 EBITDA 为 1.5T 美元，市场并未将其资本化。使用布莱克-斯科尔斯直觉，华尔街正在以边际计算成本对 24/7 数字劳动力规模的隐含波动性和右尾凸性进行定价。
@AdaniOnline，我们已经通过我们的协作式劳动力模型来实现这一现实，这是一种双轨组织架构，将人类创造力与自治人工智能代理和机器人编织到我们的公用事业、港口和运营中，每年提升 11000 多名专业人员的技能，以引领混合工业范式。

3. 1999-2020年的先例：欣快感仍然低估了政权的转变

1999 年，玛丽·米克 (Mary Meeker) 和道琼斯指数 36,000 被嘲笑为泡沫高峰错觉，当时全球电子商务约为 $150B，互联网普及率为 5%（2.77 亿用户），而 1T 美元的科技公司似乎不可能。当纳斯达克指数在 2000 年 3 月达到 5,048 点的峰值并暴跌 78%（损失约 5T 美元并破产 和 Webvan）时，传统金融宣告了这一论点的失败。
然而到了 2020 年，现实粉碎了 1999 年最疯狂的模式：4.5B+ 互联网用户（占人类的 57%）、每年 4.2T+ 的电子商务、> 60% 的数字广告份额以及核心赢家（苹果、微软、亚马逊、Alphabet）复合成 16T+ 的资产类别。传统分配者将 2000 年的清算事件误认为是上限，错过了新的数字 GDP 层。
4. 传统银行家和资本的认识论盲点
这是典型的贷款人思维正统观念：将向后看的会计比率误认为是资本创造。接受过资本稀缺银行培训的配置者崇拜尾随市盈率、静态账面价值和增量收益率——将任何打破 20 世纪电子表格的范式构建资本支出周期视为“泡沫”。

虽然传统金融在后视镜中争论记分牌，但我们已经为“智能基础设施”制定了 100B+（10 亿卢比）的路线图——掌握从端口到电力到金属到处理器的完整物理到数字堆栈，集成千兆瓦级可再生能源、电网传输和超大规模液冷人工智能数据中心（扩展到 5 吉瓦）。因为情报是用代码编写的，但它运行在电子和主权基础设施上。

印度的蓝筹股既没有被低估，也没有“落后”——它们是将人类实体经济货币化的收益工具，而那些构建能源和计算支柱的蓝筹股正在为附加合成经济的新基础提供保障。你不能用为旧世界建造的静态标尺来测量非线性尺寸（很像2000年，这里也会发生清理）。从科学角度来看，人工智能是一个更大的转变，类似于 16 世纪科学方法的发展，因此带来了更大的机会。

然而到了 2020 年，现实粉碎了 1999 年最疯狂的模式：4.5B+ 互联网用户（占人类的 57%）、每年 4.2T+ 的电子商务、> 60% 的数字广告份额以及核心赢家（苹果、微软、亚马逊、Alphabet）复合成 16T+ 的资产类别。传统分配者将 2000 年的清算事件误认为是上限，错过了新的数字 GDP 层。
4. 传统银行家和资本的认识论盲点
这是典型的贷款人思维正统观念：将向后看的会计比率误认为是资本创造。接受过资本稀缺银行培训的配置者崇拜尾随市盈率、静态账面价值和增量收益率——将任何打破 20 世纪电子表格的范式构建资本支出周期视为“泡沫”。

虽然传统金融在后视镜中争论记分牌，但我们已经为“智能基础设施”制定了 100B+（10 亿卢比）的路线图——掌握从端口到电力到金属到处理器的完整物理到数字堆栈，集成千兆瓦级可再生能源、电网传输和超大规模液冷人工智能数据中心（扩展到 5 吉瓦）。因为情报是用代码编写的，但它运行在电子和主权基础设施上。

印度的蓝筹股既没有被低估，也没有“落后”——它们是将人类实体经济货币化的收益工具，而那些构建能源和计算支柱的蓝筹股正在为附加合成经济的新基础提供保障。你不能用为旧世界建造的静态标尺来测量非线性尺寸（很像2000年，这里也会发生清理）。从科学角度来看，人工智能是一个更大的转变，类似于 16 世纪科学方法的发展，因此带来了更大的机会。

prompts.title_en: Production-Grade Fullstack .cursorrules Template for Cursor & Windsurf
prompts.scenario: 💻 编程研发 / 自动化规范
prompts.takeaway_zh: 杜绝 AI 盲目重构全量文件、使用已弃用 API 或编造虚假第三方依赖包，强制执行防御性编程与自动化单测补全。
prompts.takeaway_en: Prevents AI from hallucinating npm packages, breaking documentation, or re-writing entire files. Enforces defensive coding and unit tests.
prompts.code_snippet:
# Cursor & Windsurf Project Rules (.cursorrules)

## 1. Documentation & Code Integrity
- Maintain documentation integrity: Never strip or alter unrelated existing docstrings and comments.
- Preserving context: When modifying a function, preserve surrounding logic and existing edge-case handlers.
- Targeted replacements: Always make minimal surgical edits instead of replacing entire file contents.

## 2. Dependency & API Safety
- Strictly forbid hallucinating npm/pip packages. Only import dependencies already declared in package.json / requirements.txt.
- Verify API signatures before calling external methods. Prefer standard library solutions where feasible.

## 3. Architecture & Type Safety
- Enforce strict TypeScript / Python typing. Avoid `any` types; prefer discriminated unions and explicit return types.
- Defensive coding: Always validate external inputs and handle potential null/undefined values gracefully.

## 4. Testing & Verification Gate
- Every new core feature or bugfix must be accompanied by corresponding unit tests.
- Never declare a task complete without executing lint checks and unit tests in terminal.
prompts.usage_guide_zh: 将以上配置代码复制并保存到项目根目录下的 `.cursorrules` 文件中，Cursor 与 Windsurf 在每次生成代码和执行 Agent 任务时均会自动以此规范为最高准则约束输出。
prompts.usage_guide_en: Copy and save the above rules into `.cursorrules` in your project root directory. Cursor & Windsurf will automatically enforce these guidelines during agent coding.
prompts.summary_zh: 杜绝 AI 盲目重构全量文件、使用已弃用 API 或编造虚假第三方依赖包，强制执行防御性编程与自动化单测补全。

2. Explicitly evaluate singular points, degenerate cases, and asymptotic boundaries for convergence;
3. Steps must form a directed acyclic graph of formal lemmas without circular logic.

prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名麦肯锡级别的高级商业数据分析师，精通结构化因果归因与杜邦拆解分析。

针对我提供的 {{业务指标}} 数据，其近期出现 {{异常表现}}，请按以下框架深度剖析：
1. 【指标公式拆解】：将该指标拆分为 3~4 个下级核心因子（如转化率、客单价、复购周期），指出哪个因子波动贡献率最大；
2. 【多维下钻 (Drill-down)】：从 {{维度拆解}}（如渠道、地域、品类、新老客）分析异常聚集点；
3. 【可执行建议】：摒弃假大空的套话，给出接下来 48 小时内的 3 个立竿见影的动作与 1 个监控预警公式。
prompts.prompt_content_en: You are a senior business intelligence analyst. Dissect the metric anomaly into component drivers, perform multi-dimensional drill-down, and deliver prioritized, actionable remediation steps.

sample_output.title: 归因分析报告样本：Q3 付费转化率环比下跌 14.2%
sample_output.content:
【核心发现】：GMV 下跌 14.2% 的主要驱动因子并非流量锐减，而是【结算跳失率】从 18% 飙升至 34%。

【杜邦拆解贡献率分析】：
1. 渠道维度：自然搜索量稳定（波动 <2%），但付费投流渠道跳出率贡献了 72% 的下跌额度；
2. 终端维度：移动端 iOS 表现正常，Android Web 呈现断崖式报错，核心原因是新版本结账 SDK 在低内存机型发生闪退。

【48小时纠偏行动】：
- 动作1 (技术)：立即灰度回滚 Android 渠道结账前端包至 v2.4.1；
- 动作2 (运营)：向受影响但未支付成功的 1,420 位加购用户推送 5 元免门槛补偿券唤醒；
- 动作3 (预警)：在 Grafana 建立警报公式：`IF(Cart_to_Checkout_Ratio < 0.65, Alert_P0, Normal)`。

story mode → completed

The exact prompt and everything it found are in the replies.

viral_posts.full_text_en:
The better the harness, the better the business.

By harness I mean everything you build around the model.

It tells the agent where to get an answer, what it’s allowed to do and when to hand the work to a person. It also includes the tests you run before you change any of those rules.

That matters for two reasons.

#1 What an answer costs.

Say your agent gets 1,000 questions a day. If you can write a rule that answers 700 of them, only 300 need to go to the model. If each question costs about the same, that cuts the model bill by roughly 70%.

The hard part is knowing which 700. For that, you need somebody who does the work and can tell you when the usual rule is not applicable (exceptions).

On a logistics platform we rebuilt, AI cost about $200 per developer per month. What took time was figuring out how the old system calculated customers’ bills and which rules we needed to keep.

#2 What the company gets to keep.

Take the patient-billing voice agent we built for a US healthtech startup. It can give a patient the correct balance and still handle the call badly.

> Did it verify who was on the phone first?
> If the patient disputed the charge, did it hand the call to staff?
> If it scheduled a follow-up, did it check non-working hours when the message actually went out?

Those decisions are part of the harness. The system ran 13,650 tests on every pull request. In production, it handled 61,246 calls, and about 97% of patient conversations finished without a human stepping in.

The company-specific IP is clearest in the exceptions.

When an experienced billing lead explains why two calls that sound alike need different handling, you can turn that distinction into a rule and save both cases as tests.

Now the next engineer can change the workflow, or try a different model, and check whether it still makes the call the billing lead would make.

Your competitor can rent the same model, but they still have to learn which exceptions matter and what to do about each one.

If you run a software company adding AI this year, I’d put the budget there first. Sit with the people who handle the exceptions. Write down how they decide. Give the model the work that still needs judgment.
viral_posts.full_text_zh:
线束越好，生意就越好。

我所说的“利用”是指围绕模型构建的一切。

它告诉代理在哪里获得答案、允许做什么以及何时将工作交给某人。它还包括您在更改任何这些规则之前运行的测试。

这很重要有两个原因。

#1 一个答案的成本是多少。

假设您的代理每天收到 1,000 个问题。如果您可以编写一条规则来回答其中 700 个问题，则只需将 300 个问题转入模型即可。如果每个问题的成本大致相同，那么模型费用就会减少大约 70%。

困难的部分是知道是哪个 700。为此，您需要有人来完成这项工作，并且可以告诉您何时不适用通常的规则（例外情况）。

在我们重建的物流平台上，每个开发人员每月的人工智能成本约为 200 美元。需要时间的是弄清楚旧系统如何计算客户的账单以及我们需要遵守哪些规则。

#2 公司可以保留什么。

以我们为美国一家医疗科技初创公司构建的患者计费语音代理为例。它可以给病人提供正确的平衡，但仍然不能很好地处理呼叫。

> 它是否首先验证了谁在打电话？
> 如果患者对收费提出异议，是否会将电话转交给工作人员？
> 如果安排了后续行动，当消息实际发出时，它是否检查了非工作时间？

这些决定是安全带的一部分。系统对每个拉取请求运行了 13,650 次测试。在生产中，它处理了 61,246 个电话，大约 97% 的患者对话在没有人工介入的情况下完成。

公司特定的 IP 在例外情况中最为清晰。

当经验丰富的计费主管解释为什么两个听起来相似的呼叫需要不同的处理时，您可以将这种区别转化为规则并将这两种情况保存为测试。

现在，下一位工程师可以更改工作流程，或尝试不同的模型，并检查它是否仍会拨打计费主管会拨打的电话。

您的竞争对手可以租用相同的型号，但他们仍然必须了解哪些例外情况很重要以及如何处理每种例外情况。

如果你今年经营一家添加人工智能的软件公司，我会把预算放在第一位。与处理例外情况的人坐在一起。写下他们如何决定。给模型一些仍然需要判断的工作。

viral_posts.full_text_en:
The AI-powered judges didn't move house. Their paperwork did.

That's why @GenLayer's move to @arbitrum Nitro deserves closer inspection.

The GenLayer Chain records transaction order, validator committees, votes, appeals, staking and final outcomes. That coordination layer transitioned from Matter Labs' ZK Stack to Arbitrum Nitro.

Adjudication itself remains unchanged. Optimistic Democracy still has validators using different AI models to evaluate disputes. GenVM still executes intelligent contracts on their nodes.

Where was the engineering?

At the boundaries: the bridge, Ethereum integration, and gas-cost accounting.

One broken handoff could leave a perfectly sound verdict stranded inside a functioning network. That is the practical risk behind a technical migration announcement.

A meaningful migration test happens where systems interface, not where screenshots look reassuring.

A release note reading "new stack" matters less than "nothing broke."

If an AI agent wins an appeal but the app never receives the result, would you blame the judgment process or the chain underneath? Why?
viral_posts.full_text_zh:
人工智能法官没有搬家。他们的文书工作做到了。

这就是为什么 @GenLayer 转向 @arbitrum Nitro 值得仔细检查。

GenLayer Chain 记录交易顺序、验证人委员会、投票、申诉、质押和最终结果。该协调层从 Matter Labs 的 ZK Stack 过渡到 Arbitrum Nitro。

裁决本身保持不变。乐观民主仍然有验证者使用不同的人工智能模型来评估争议。 GenVM 仍然在其节点上执行智能合约。

工程在哪里？

边界：桥梁、以太坊集成和天然气成本核算。

一次故障的切换可能会使完美无缺的判决滞留在正常运行的网络中。这就是技术迁移公告背后的实际风险。

有意义的迁移测试发生在系统接口的地方，而不是屏幕截图看起来令人放心的地方。

发布说明中写着“新堆栈”比“没有任何问题”更重要。

如果人工智能代理赢得了上诉，但应用程序从未收到结果，你会责怪判断过程还是底层的链条？为什么？

🇪🇺 The EU, the world’s strictest data cop, just got hit by a cyberattack.

The European Commission says it responded to a “detected cyber campaign,” and Politico reports that large amounts of personal data may have been compromised.

Systems for payslips, HR and medical reimbursements were knocked offline for about 10 days.

And the EU isn’t the only one. In the past week alone:

•⁠  ⁠The U.S. was hit by 5 major outages in under a week, from Microsoft 365 to United flights to Chase and Wells Fargo. Officials insist they’re a coincidence.
•⁠  ⁠Hackers hijacked Optimizely to plant malicious code on 178 major websites, including CNN, Zoom, HSBC and IKEA.
•⁠  ⁠Hackers compromised one of Microsoft’s AI agent software packages to push a credential stealer.
•⁠  ⁠TSMC confirmed a data breach that exposed employee information.

Either it’s the busiest week in hacker history, or the AI agents have officially escaped…

Sources: Politico, Reuters, The Hill, The Hacker News, Check Point / Writer: Julie

viral_posts.full_text_en:
Imagine you have an AI agent helping you prepare a market research report.

It has gathered information, compared competitors and organized most of the findings.

But there’s a problem.

It needs fresh market data, and that’s something it isn’t equipped to collect on its own.

Another AI agent specializes in exactly that.

Now, instead of abandoning the task, the first agent needs a way to find the second, request its service, agree on the job and receive the completed data.

The second agent does the work, submits the result, and gets paid once the delivery is verified.

Two agents, different capabilities with one completed task.

This is the kind of interaction that makes agent-to-agent commerce interesting.

But for this to happen reliably, agents need infrastructure for service discovery, bidding, identity, reputation, escrow and settlement.

That’s what @termix_ai is working towards with AACP.

Through https://t.co/Z7DbQJlA2K, agents can list services, discover opportunities, take on jobs and participate in an economy built around actual work.

I think one of the biggest developments in the AI space won’t just be how much an individual agent can accomplish.

It’ll be what becomes possible when different agents can work together.

Explore the marketplace: https://t.co/lGui8LIpKw

Read about AACP: https://t.co/NZXKULTjFB

但有一个问题。

它需要新鲜的市场数据，而这是它自己无法收集的。

另一位人工智能代理正是专门从事这一领域的工作。

现在，第一个代理需要一种方法来找到第二个代理、请求其服务、同意工作并接收已完成的数据，而不是放弃任务。

第二个代理完成工作，提交结果，并在交付验证后获得报酬。

两名特工，具有不同的能力，但完成一项任务。

这种互动使得代理商之间的商务变得有趣。

但为了可靠地实现这一点，代理商需要用于服务发现、投标、身份、声誉、托管和结算的基础设施。

这就是 @termix_ai 与 AACP 共同努力的目标。

通过 ，代理商可以列出服务、发现机会、接受工作并参与围绕实际工作建立的经济。

我认为人工智能领域最大的发展之一不仅仅是单个代理可以完成多少工作。
